title: EvidenceCertificate
description: The signable, verifiable claim about ONE confirmed finding. This schema reflects the ACTUAL serialized (model_dump(mode="json")) shape of framework.v2.evidence.models.EvidenceCertificate. It is fully deterministic (no wall-clock; `seq` is the monotonic order), so its canonical bytes are stable across producer and verifier. The certificate's canonical form is the sha256 preimage of its `cert_digest` and of the m-of-n governance signature over it (under the `crucible-evidence-v1\u0000` domain tag). The three additive members `report_claims`, `oracle_version`, and `how_to_verify` are DROPPED from the serialized form when empty (a model_serializer wrap), so a certificate built without them hashes and signs BYTE-IDENTICALLY to a pre-additive certificate. `additionalProperties:false` mirrors the model's `extra="forbid"`.

schema_version.description: 1 for a plain certificate; 2 when it carries `report_claims`.

finding_ref.description: check_id / finding slug. The only member with no default.

bug_class.description: The oracle-provable class the certificate asserts. Default "".

confirmed_by.description: The oracle kind that fired. Default "".

oracle_context_digest.description: sha256 (bare lowercase hex) of the canonical oracle_context the oracle adjudicated. The signature cannot be lifted onto different evidence: a verifier recomputes digest_payload(oracle_context) and requires equality (the BINDING layer).

artifacts.description: Per-file sha256 manifest of the raw on-disk evidence the oracle saw, sorted by relative path. May be empty (a certificate then verifies on reproduction + binding alone).

seq.description: Monotonic order (NOT a wall-clock) — the chain links certificates in this order.

report_claims.description: ADDITIVE (schema v2). Atomic report sentences bound into (and signed with) the certificate. DROPPED from the serialized form when null/empty, so an older certificate is byte-identical. When present it is sorted by (sentence, bug_class) for deterministic canonical bytes.

oracle_version.description: ADDITIVE. The content-derived id@version of the oracle that fired, stamped at mint time (thus signed). DROPPED from the serialized form when "". A verifier compares it to the current oracle version to detect a stale proof (the oracle body changed since issue).

how_to_verify.description: ADDITIVE. A deterministic per-finding 'how to verify / test / patch' note (surface + firing oracle + class remediation). DROPPED from the serialized form when "". Signed when present, so it travels tamper-evident.

ArtifactRef.description: One raw evidence file, bound by digest so the certificate proves WHICH bytes it was judged on.

path.description: Relative to the engagement evidence root. MUST be relative and MUST NOT contain a '..' component (rejected at parse time and re-confined at verify time).

sha256.description: Bare lowercase hex sha256 of the file bytes.

ReportClaim.description: One report sentence bound into the certificate. Its text is tamper-evident because the whole certificate is signed. A `render_as == "fact"` claim is additionally re-admitted through the veracity firewall by the VIGIL verifier (framework-specific).

render_as.description: The producer's claim; verify re-derives fact truth and never trusts the label for grounding.
